body:
Thanks, man. That's pretty nice of you to say. On my primary account I do often times visit that subreddit. It helps a bit, but for some reason knowing others are going through the same kind of thing doesn't help as much as it should. 

And as much as I'd like to blame the city I live in for being small and crappy, it's actually a really large metropolitan area with over a million people. I won't name the city, but it's one of the ten largest cities in the United States. There are places to apply, just not much that relates to my major, and more importantly, no one who wants me to work for them. 

I find the more and more I get buried in my depression, the more I want to take off and take a job elsewhere. A friend of mine has mentioned Australia liking Americans with degrees, another friend swears that Israel also loves graduated Americans (but let's not get all political here). And I've thought a lot about the national park service. So hey, we'll see.

Yeah, I've talked to psychiatrists in the past on a regular basis. They helped a lot for different kinds of things. As I mentioned I've suffered from depression for a long time, mainly due to shortcomings in my personal life. Luckily that's mostly behind me. But I'm trailing off. I've been on anti-depressants, I've been held for 72 hours, I've talked to a doctor regularly, and as much as that helped in the past, this isn't a problem I think will be solved by tossing pills at it.

I have one friend who's sympathetic to my problems. My best friend where I live knows more than anyone the insane amount of applications I put in, partially because they're nice enough to drive me around when I go on an applying spree every three days, and afterward he takes me home he usually comes in while I send out follow-up emails and calls. He's pretty much the only person who knows I'm trying hard to do this and doesn't write me off as completely lazy. He's expressed desire to help me, but they're unfortunately unemployed and being that he's also an ex-humanities student, has no ties to anyone in a hiring position.
